CRITICAL OWNER LOGIN FAILURE — FIX THE REAL MOBILE FLOW END TO END

THE PREVIOUS “OWNER SIGN-IN VERIFIED” REPORT IS INVALID.

The real production phone test still returns:

message: Invalid login credentials
code: invalid_credentials
HTTP status: 400
type: AuthApiError

Do not produce another PASS report until the exact phone login shown in production succeeds.

SECURITY FIRST

1. The owner password was exposed in screenshots and reports.
2. Immediately redact it from:
   - chat output
   - logs
   - reports
   - screenshots
   - test fixtures
   - source code
   - environment debugging
3. Require the owner to rotate the exposed password through a secure password-reset flow.
4. Never print or persist the replacement password.
5. Do not place passwords in agent-state.json, console logs, database tables, Git history, or API responses.

==================================================
STEP 1 — IDENTIFY THE EXACT PRODUCTION AUTH TARGET
==================================================

From the real Android/web login screen, capture without exposing secrets:

- app version
- source commit
- runtime platform
- current route
- Supabase project URL hostname
- Supabase project reference
- API base URL
- environment name
- owner email after trim/lowercase
- authentication method called
- exact source file and function called by Sign In

Confirm whether the phone is using:

- production Supabase
- staging Supabase
- an old Supabase project
- an old APK configuration
- a cached OTA bundle
- a server proxy endpoint
- direct supabase.auth.signInWithPassword()

Required proof:

Mobile Supabase project ref:
Server Supabase project ref:
Expected production project ref:
Mobile API URL:
Live commit:
APK version:
Authentication source file:
Authentication function:

PASS only if the phone and server point to the same intended production project.

==================================================
STEP 2 — STOP USING A DIFFERENT TEST PATH
==================================================

The previous report may have tested an API endpoint, server-side token flow, passwordless flow, service-role flow, or another environment.

Run the exact production mobile code path:

supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({
  email: normalizedOwnerEmail,
  password: userEnteredPassword
})

Do not:

- substitute a JWT
- use service-role authentication
- reuse an existing session
- use a magic link
- use an admin-generated token
- inject a test session
- call an internal endpoint that bypasses the mobile client
- claim success based only on /health

Log only safe metadata:

- timestamp
- project reference
- email hash or masked email
- method name
- response status
- error code
- user ID after success
- session method
- app version
- commit SHA

Never log the password.

==================================================
STEP 3 — VERIFY THE OWNER USER IN SUPABASE AUTH
==================================================

Using the exact production Supabase project:

- confirm the owner user exists
- confirm the normalized email matches exactly
- confirm the account is not duplicated
- confirm email identity exists
- confirm email confirmation status
- confirm the user is not banned
- confirm the user is not soft-deleted
- confirm the owner role mapping exists
- confirm user metadata does not override access incorrectly
- confirm there are no two owner accounts with capitalization differences
- confirm password authentication is enabled
- confirm the account belongs to the same Supabase project used by the phone

Return safe evidence:

User exists: yes/no
User ID:
Normalized email:
Email confirmed: yes/no
Banned: yes/no
Deleted: yes/no
Identity provider:
Owner role source:
Supabase project reference:

Do not expose password hashes, access tokens, refresh tokens, service keys, or secrets.

==================================================
STEP 4 — ROTATE THE EXPOSED PASSWORD SECURELY
==================================================

Because the password was displayed publicly in screenshots:

1. Trigger the official secure password-reset flow.
2. Owner sets a new private password directly.
3. Do not ask the owner to paste the new password into Rork chat.
4. Do not print the new password.
5. Revoke old sessions after the reset.
6. Confirm the old exposed password fails.
7. Confirm the new password succeeds only through the real phone UI.

Required tests:

- old password → rejected
- new password → accepted
- invalid password → rejected
- refresh token → valid after new login
- previous sessions → revoked if configured

==================================================
STEP 5 — AUDIT MOBILE CONFIGURATION
==================================================

Inspect the final mobile build configuration:

- app.config
- app.json
- eas.json
- Expo public environment variables
- native build environment
- production release profile
- Android package configuration
- runtimeVersion
- update channel
- embedded bundle
- OTA update channel
- Supabase client initialization
- API client initialization

Search for:

- old Supabase URLs
- old anonymous keys
- staging URLs
- localhost
- temporary tunnels
- Vercel test endpoints
- Rork test endpoints
- duplicate Supabase clients
- hard-coded owner email
- hidden whitespace
- cached environment values
- fallback test configuration

Return every discovered auth configuration source and indicate which one the running APK actually uses.

==================================================
STEP 6 — FIX INPUT HANDLING WITHOUT MODIFYING PASSWORD
==================================================

Email may be:

- trimmed
- lowercased

Password must be:

- preserved exactly
- not trimmed
- not lowercased
- not normalized
- not transformed
- not replaced
- not auto-filled from an old stored value
- not overwritten by passwordless state

Verify:

- keyboard input
- secure text field state
- React state value length
- no invisible newline
- no trailing space insertion
- password visibility toggle does not modify state
- Remember Me does not replace the password
- form submit uses the latest state
- no stale closure
- no double submission
- no magic-link handler overwriting the password flow

Do not log the password value. Log only its character count and whether the state changed.

==================================================
STEP 7 — REMOVE PASSWORDLESS INTERFERENCE
==================================================

The previous report references passwordless login and magic-link state.

Audit and isolate:

- password sign-in
- magic-link sign-in
- OTP sign-in
- session recovery
- deep-link processing
- cached authentication state

Rules:

- Selecting password login must call only signInWithPassword.
- Magic-link state must not modify the password.
- A prior passwordless session must not automatically replace the current login method.
- Logout must clear local session state.
- App restart must restore only a valid session.
- Invalid or expired sessions must return to the login screen.

Remove any logic that reports `passwordPreserved=true` without proving the real mobile password request succeeded.

==================================================
STEP 8 — COMPARE DIRECT SUPABASE AND APP REQUESTS
==================================================

Against the same production project and newly rotated password, test:

A. Direct controlled client test
B. Production web login screen
C. Final Android APK login screen
D. Production API login endpoint, only if the app actually uses it

For each test show:

Platform
Project reference
Method
Timestamp
HTTP status
Error code
User ID on success
Session issued
Result

All successful tests must return the same owner user ID.

If direct Supabase succeeds but the phone fails:
- mobile state/configuration is defective.

If both fail:
- account/password/project identity is defective.

If API succeeds but direct mobile fails:
- the API test is not equivalent and cannot be used as proof.

==================================================
STEP 9 — FIX OWNER AUTHORIZATION AFTER AUTHENTICATION
==================================================

After password login succeeds, separately verify authorization:

- owner user ID
- owner email
- owner role
- Owner Dashboard
- Admin Hub
- Settings
- Variables
- Audit Log
- protected API routes
- non-owner rejection

Authentication success and owner authorization are separate tests.

Do not claim owner login is fixed merely because an API returned a JWT.

==================================================
STEP 10 — BUILD A NEW PRODUCTION APK
==================================================

After fixing the exact source:

- increment version
- increment versionCode
- create a new production APK
- embed the correct production configuration
- remove old OTA/cache ambiguity
- publish the APK under the owner-controlled GitHub Release
- provide SHA-256
- provide source commit
- provide EAS build ID
- provide direct APK link

The old APK cannot be reused as proof after authentication code or environment configuration changes.

Required output:

APK filename:
Version:
Version code:
Package ID:
Source commit:
EAS build ID:
SHA-256:
Direct APK URL:
GitHub Release URL:

==================================================
STEP 11 — PHYSICAL PHONE TEST
==================================================

Install the new APK as a fresh installation on the physical Android phone.

Before testing:

- uninstall the previous IVX build
- clear old app data
- verify the new version
- verify the production project reference safely
- do not reuse an old session

Test:

1. Launch app.
2. Enter owner email manually.
3. Enter the newly rotated password privately.
4. Tap Sign In.
5. Confirm no HTTP 400.
6. Confirm owner identity.
7. Open Owner Dashboard.
8. Open Admin Hub.
9. Open Settings.
10. Open Variables.
11. Close app completely.
12. Reopen app.
13. Confirm session persistence.
14. Log out.
15. Confirm protected routes are blocked.
16. Enter wrong password.
17. Confirm rejection.
18. Enter correct password again.
19. Confirm successful second login.
20. Test a non-owner account and confirm 403 for owner routes.

Required evidence:

- device model
- Android version
- APK version
- commit SHA
- timestamps
- screen recording
- safe auth logs
- pass/fail matrix

Do not expose the password in the recording.

==================================================
STEP 12 — CORRECT THE FALSE QA RECORD
==================================================

Update the previous QA report:

Previous status:
VERIFIED

Correct status:
FAILED / INVALIDATED

Reason:
The real production mobile UI returned Supabase AuthApiError invalid_credentials, HTTP 400.

Document:

- why the earlier test produced a false PASS
- which environment/path it tested
- why it differed from the phone
- exact code correction
- exact configuration correction
- new commit
- new APK
- new physical-device evidence

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE RULE
==================================================

Owner authentication may be marked VERIFIED only when:

- the exposed password has been rotated
- the phone uses the intended production Supabase project
- the exact mobile signInWithPassword path succeeds
- owner identity is confirmed
- owner routes open
- invalid passwords fail
- non-owner users are rejected
- session persistence works
- logout works
- a fresh production APK passes on a physical Android device
- the password is absent from all logs and reports

Until then, report:

OWNER LOGIN STATUS: FAILED
PRODUCTION STATUS: PARTIAL

Start with project/environment comparison and secure password rotation now.
Do not return another narrative PASS report.
